question: True or false: an Irish famine a century before the Great Famine may have killed a larger share of the people?
answer: True. In the Great Frost of 1739–40 potatoes froze in the ground and in storage pits, and a cold, wet year followed. Estimates put deaths in 1740–41 at 13% to 20% of about 2.4 million people, against roughly 12% in 1845–52. Irish speakers called it Bliain an Áir, the year of slaughter.
move: The disaster everyone remembers is not always the worst of its kind.
trap: False, since the 1840s famine is the one every history names.

diagram.caption: Share of the people who died: the forgotten famine may have been worse.

reference: Dickson, Arctic Ireland: The Extraordinary Story of the Great Frost and Forgotten Famine of 1740-41, White Row Press, 1997
